title: Adaptive ingest proxy with schema negotiation and trace anchoring
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Current structured-log ingest paths accept a variety of producer schemas and rely on downstream pipelines to normalize fields. This causes brittle joins to traces, inconsistent correlation_id placement, and frequent consumer-side parsing errors that spike retries and increase tail latency. We need a tenant-aware edge component that: negotiates/validates schema versions with producers, anchors trace/correlation IDs into a canonical field set early, and provides deterministic buffering/backpressure so downstream Loki/ELK tails are protected from noisy tenants.

Goals:
- Reduce parsing-errors and downstream retries by validating and mapping producer schemas at the edge.
- Ensure every structured event includes a canonical trace_anchor and correlation_id so logs join cleanly to traces and metrics.
- Provide per-tenant adaptive buffering/backpressure and rate smoothing to avoid overload cascades into storage and query backends.

Non-goals:
- Replacing full-service schema registry (this work will integrate with the existing registry but not implement a brand-new global registry).
- Full reindexing/migration of historical logs; we are focused on ingest-path correctness and forward compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: Edge proxy negotiates schema version with producer via X-Schema-Version header and rejects >95% malformed envelopes with descriptive error code 400+X
All accepted structured events are transformed to include canonical fields: trace_anchor, correlation_id, tenant_id, schema_version
Deterministic fanout to Loki/ELK retains original event_id and adds ingest_metadata with upstream processing latency
Per-tenant buffer prevents downstream queue growth beyond configured SLO; documented behavior when tenant exceeds burst allowances

Unit and integration tests cover schema probing, mapping rules, trace anchoring, and failure modes; end-to-end benchmark shows <=10% tail-latency increase at 90th percentile under synthetic cross-tenant spike compared to current baseline
Console dashboard adds ingest_metrics: malformed_rate, anchor_missing_rate, per-tenant_buffer_occupancy, stalls and drop_reason breakdowns
implementation_steps: Spike: implement lightweight schema probe in a local envoy wasm filter and validate with 4 internal producers (done)
Define canonical mapping spec and field precedence for trace/correlation fields (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proxy/pull/178)
Implement mapping + trace_anchor enrichment in ingest-proxy; add tenant-priority buffer with configurable thresholds
Instrument metrics and logs for buffer occupancy, rejection reasons, and mapping latencies
Add integration tests against a Loki dev cluster and an Elasticsearch staging cluster
Rollout plan: shadow mode for 2 weeks (no rejects) -> canary (10% of tenants) -> full rollout; include automatic rollback if malformed_rate or tail_latency increases beyond thresholds
notes: Trade-offs discussed: doing mapping at the edge adds CPU cost and a small latency tax but prevents expensive downstream retries and reduces overall cost by lowering wasted work. Alternate considered: only tagging trace_anchor in the runtime, but that leaves malformed payloads to downstream services and complicates tenant-based backpressure. We decided to perform best-effort normalization at the edge and surface unfixable events to a quarantine sink for offline processing.
comments: 2025-09-15 Aisha Patel: Created ticket and attached spike notes. Initial performance spike shows 8-12ms additional p99 per-event in wasm-based mapping on small instances.
2025-09-22 Tomás Rivera: Completed envoy-wasm probe. Observed malformed_rate from test producers drop from 4.1% -> 0.6% when mapping rules applied. Uploaded mapping spec to Drive link.

2025-09-28 Engineering review: Feedback from SRE (J. Huang) — add explicit backpressure signal header X-Ingest-Retry-After for producers and document expected retry semantics. Also add per-tenant memory cap to avoid OOMs.

2025-09-30 Security review kickoff: requested threat model for header injection and tenant spoofing; agreed to require tenant-signed tokens on initial handshake and validate via control-plane service before enabling strict rejects.

2025-10-02 Tomás Rivera: Implemented buffer eviction policy (LRU per-tenant) and added prometheus metrics. PR 178 opened. Running staging load test targeting 10k eps with mixed schema producers. Observed 7% p99 delta vs baseline; spike on very wide events still triggers quarantine path — working on optimizing map code path.
FOLLOW-UP: Coordinate with console team to add ingest_metrics panel before canary rollout. PM to notify top 50 tenants about canary window and provide opt-out link.
